newsitem.title: USA: Orlando, Florida airport sees cargo gains.
newsitem.headline: Orlando, Florida airport sees cargo gains.

text.p: Despite a disappointing year so far, Orlando International Airport expects to see a 3 percent to 5 percent increase in cargo volumes during the winter months, an airport executive said Thursday.

"I don't think the growth will be in the double digits like in the past, but we will see a nice upturn, in the range of 3 percent to 5 percent," said Ken St. Amand, cargo marketing manager, told Reuters in an interview.

In June, 19,406 tons of cargo moved through Orlando International, 4.75 percent less than June of 1995. In July, cargo volume was 18,169 tons, up 2.81 percent. For the first seven months of the year cargo volumes were off 3.98 percent.
Some of Orlando's biggest carriers switched from wide-body aircraft to narrow-body, decreasing cargo capacity and hurting cargo volumes, St. Amand said.
The opening of nearby Sanford Airport, which handles only charter airlines, also took away some cargo, he said.
